newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures fall in tandem with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures fall in tandem with cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mostly lower Wednesday in tandem with softer cash market prices tied to lackluster power demand in the western U.S., industry sources said.
While electricity usage in the West continued to decline this week due to cool weather, surplus supply of hydropower was still available, they said.
As a sign of ample hydroelectric output in the Northwest, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) today expanded offers of off-peak power in the Southwest.
October California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished down 16 cents at $16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing in a 20 cent range.
November COB ended up four cents at $16.49 after trading between $16.30 and $16.50. Other active COB months settled mixed.
October Palo Verde (PV) futures, the only active only in that half of the complex, finished down 10 cents at $16.55 after reaching as low as $16.40.
NYMEX estimated 279 COB and 11 PV contracts were sold.
